summary: Ran the AI support pricing-accuracy check (scripts/test_ai_support_pricing.js) 3 separate times against the real OpenAI model at temperature 0.2. All 12 case runs passed (4/4 in each run, exit code 0 every time). Domain+cPanel total: confirmed about $105 = domain from $30 + Premium HostPanel $75/month, and never said '$75/week'. Trap question: always answered 'No', with $30/week for the 1-Week plan and $75/month for the HostPanel. Plan listing: all 3 plans with the correct periods ($30/week, $75/month, $100/month). Marketplace: $30–$3,000 every time. No crashes or errors. Code review confirmed getUserContext() is still called in buildAiMessages (line ~1625), the canonical pricing table reads its prices from env (PREMIUM_ANTIRED_WEEKLY_PRICE=30, PREMIUM_ANTIRED_CPANEL_PRICE=75, GOLDEN_ANTIRED_CPANEL_PRICE=100, MIN_DOMAIN_PRICE=30), and temperatures are 0.2 for getAiResponse, streaming and marketplace, and 0.1 for moderation.

minor.issue: In run 1, the 'list hosting plans' answer repeated an internal prompt rule to the customer: 'Note: Do NOT confuse the $75 monthly plan with a weekly plan — $75 is monthly only.' Not factually wrong, but it reads like system text. Suggest adding a prompt line telling the model never to repeat the anti-confusion rules word for word to the customer.

The $30–$3,000 range is typed in by hand in the prompt (lines 91, 527, 535, 563) instead of reading MIN_PRICE/MAX_PRICE from js/marketplace-service.js. The two match today but could drift apart if the constants change.

action_items: Optional: tell the model not to repeat the internal anti-confusion rules to customers (seen once in 3 runs)

Prompt marketplace range is typed in by hand (drift risk)

seed_data_creation: None. The script uses chatIds qa_pricing_1..4 and clears their history before each case.
